featured_videos.title: This Will Be Your New Favorite Keto Dessert!
featured_videos.creator: Keto Twins
featured_videos.editorial_title: Keto Ice Cream Bars That Actually Work
featured_videos.commentary: The Keto Twins dropped a keto dessert video that hit 20K views, and the comment section turned into a full-on recipe laboratory. People aren't just watching, they're riffing: raspberry dark chocolate chip versions, orange creamsicle variations, and one person who's been using allulose as their secret weapon for ice cream that doesn't turn into a brick in the freezer. Watch it here and honestly, bookmark the comments too. The real value is the community figuring out what actually works.

featured_videos.title: Keto Flu or Toxic Additives? The Truth About LMNT, Re-Lyte, & Keto Chow
featured_videos.creator: Dr. Tony Hampton - The Metabolic Health Doc
featured_videos.editorial_title: What's Actually in Your Electrolyte Packets?
featured_videos.commentary: Dr. Tony Hampton does something really valuable here. He pulls apart the ingredient lists of LMNT, Re-Lyte, and Keto Chow side by side and asks the question most of us skip: what else are you swallowing besides sodium and potassium? The comments are telling. People sharing stories about maltodextrin hiding in "natural flavors," others landing in the ER from potassium overdoses, and plenty who ditched the packets entirely for DIY salt water and feel better. If you're spending $45 a month on electrolyte products, this is 22 minutes that could save you money and maybe a trip to urgent care.

featured_videos.title: What We Actually Order on Keto When We Eat Out
featured_videos.creator: Keto Twins
featured_videos.editorial_title: How to Eat Keto at Any Restaurant
featured_videos.commentary: If you've ever panicked at a restaurant menu while your friends order pasta, this one's for you. The Keto Twins walk through real-world ordering at Mexican spots, sushi bars, pizza places, and Chinese buffets, and the 141 comments are basically a crowdsourced survival guide. The video is practical and honest, including the tip to eat before you go to certain events. The hidden gem in the comments: someone warning that many wing places coat their wings in corn starch before frying, and you'd never know just by looking.

featured_videos.title: "Low Protein Diet Was Actually The Healthiest"
featured_videos.creator: Kent Carnivore
featured_videos.editorial_title: The Low-Protein Myth Gets a Reality Check
featured_videos.commentary: Kent Carnivore tackles the claim that low-protein diets produce the best health outcomes. It's a claim that keeps resurfacing in vegan and fruitarian circles, and Kent breaks down why the studies behind it don't hold up when you look at body composition, muscle retention, and metabolic markers. The comment section is full of people sharing their own n=1 results, including one commenter doing 150 pullups at age 50 after three decades of high-protein eating. The protein debate matters because too many people are still scared of eating enough, and that fear keeps them underfed and losing muscle.

featured_videos.title: Finding Love During My Carnivore Weight Loss Journey
featured_videos.creator: Ground Beef Chief
featured_videos.editorial_title: Week 74: When Carnivore Results Go Beyond the Scale
featured_videos.commentary: Ground Beef Chief is 74 weeks into his carnivore journey, and this video tells you everything about what consistency actually produces. The numbers are small (1,884 views) but the comment-to-view ratio is 9.2%, which is borderline unheard of. That's not an algorithm win. That's a community that watched someone transform and now genuinely cares about the guy's life. When your weight loss journey brings enough confidence to put yourself out there again, that's a result no scale can measure.

featured_videos.title: This Carnivore System Is a Game Changer
featured_videos.creator: Chris Cooking Nashville
featured_videos.editorial_title: A Practical Carnivore Cooking System That Works
featured_videos.commentary: Chris Cooking Nashville addresses the number one reason people quit carnivore: they get bored eating the same three things. His approach is building a repeatable cooking system rather than chasing individual recipes, which is honestly how most long-term carnivore people stay consistent. The engagement on this one is strong for a smaller channel. People are preordering his cookbook, which tells you the audience is hungry for practical, day-to-day guidance instead of another "eat steak and eggs" video.
